spots.name: Kaunas Castle

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sun

spots.summary: Kaunas Castle is a medieval castle in Kaunas, the second-largest city in Lithuania. Archeological evidence suggests that it was built during the mid-14th century in the Gothic style. Its site is strategic—a rise on the banks of the Nemunas River near its confluence with the Neris River.

spots.name: Ninth Fort
spots.summary: The Ninth Fort is a stronghold in the northern part of Šilainiai elderate, Kaunas, Lithuania. It is a part of the Kaunas Fortress, built in the late 19th century. During the Soviet occupation, the fort was used as a prison and way-station for prisoners being transported to labour camps.

spots.name: Kaunas Mosque
spots.summary: The Kaunas Mosque is a World Heritage-listed Sunni Islamic mosque, located at Tatars Street 6, in the Centras eldership of Kaunas, Lithuania. It is the only mosque in the Kaunas district, one of only four mosques in Lithuania, and the only brick mosque in Lithuania and the Baltic countries.

spots.name: Kaunas Fortress

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Kaunas Fortress is the remains of a fortress complex in Kaunas, Lithuania. It was constructed and renovated between 1882 and 1915 to protect the Russian Empire's western borders, and was designated a "first-class" fortress in 1887.

spots.name: Žmuidzinavičius Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Žmuidzinavičius Museum, also known as the Devil Museum, is a museum in Kaunas, Lithuania, dedicated to collecting and exhibiting sculptures and carvings of devils from all over the world. The museum is a part of M. K. Čiurlionis National Art Museum.

spots.name: Pažaislis Monastery

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sun

spots.summary: Pažaislis Monastery and the Church of the Visitation form the largest monastery complex in Lithuania, and the most renowned example of Baroque architecture in the country. The church is the most marble-decorated Baroque church of the former Grand Duchy of Lithuania.

names.ja: パジャイスリス修道院

spots.name: Church of St. Francis Xavier

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of St. Francis Xavier is a Roman Catholic church located in the Old Town of Kaunas, Lithuania. The church, dedicated to St. Francis Xavier, was built in the Rotušės square by Jesuits. The Jesuits opened their first residence in Kaunas in 1642 and established a chapel in the House of Perkūnas in 1643.

spots.summary: Church of Vytautas the Great or the Church of the Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary is a Roman Catholic church in the Old Town of Kaunas, Lithuania, and is the oldest church in the city and an important example of Gothic architecture in Lithuania, having the only Gothic cross-shaped plan in Lithuania.

spots.name: Christ's Resurrection Church
spots.summary: Kaunas our Lord Jesus Christ's Resurrection Basilica is a monumental Roman Catholic minor basilica in Kaunas, Lithuania. The church was consecrated in 2004, and in 2005 it was finally completed. It is the largest basilical church in the Baltic states.

names.fr: Basilique de la Résurrection du Christ de Kaunas

spots.name: Church of St. George
spots.summary: St. George the Martyr Church, Kaunas is a Roman Catholic church in the Old Town of Kaunas, Lithuania, which stands in front of the Kaunas Castle. It is a prominent example of Gothic architecture in Lithuania.

spots.summary: The Kaunas Synagogue, also known as the Choral Ohel Yaakov Synagogue, is an Orthodox Jewish congregation and synagogue, located at 13 East Ožeškienės Street, in Centras eldership, Kaunas, in the Kaunas County of Lithuania.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Church of St. Gertrude is located in the Old Town of Kaunas and is one of the oldest Brick Gothic churches and buildings of Gothic architecture in Lithuania.

spots.name: Freedom Monument
spots.summary: The Freedom Monument in Kaunas, Lithuania, by sculptor Juozas Zikaras, was unveiled in 1928 on the occasion of the 10th anniversary of the reestablishment of the independence of Lithuania. At that time, Kaunas was the temporary capital of the state.

photo.author: Original uploader was Algirdas at lt.wikipedia

spots.name: Freedom Warrior
spots.summary: The Freedom Warrior is a public sculpture in Kaunas, Lithuania. It is inspired by Vytis, a national symbol of Lithuania.

spots.name: Kaunas Carillon

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Kaunas Carillon is a carillon in the tower of the Vytautas the Great War Museum in Kaunas, Lithuania. The carillon officially belongs to the Ministry of National Defence of the Republic of Lithuania and Vytautas the Great War Museum.

spots.name: Seventh Fort

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Wed

spots.summary: The Seventh Fort or VII Fort is a defensive fortification built in Žaliakalnis district of Kaunas, Lithuania, during implementation of the first phase of the construction of the Kaunas Fortress. It is located near the Hospital of Lithuanian University of Health Sciences.

spots.summary: Darius and Girėnas stadium is a multi-use stadium in Kaunas, Lithuania. With a seating capacity of 15,026, it is the largest stadium in Lithuania and the Baltic states. Located in the Ąžuolynas park in Žaliakalnis district, it serves as a venue for football matches, athletic competitions, and other events.

spots.name: Old Kaunas Ducal Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Old Kaunas Ducal Palace is a building complex at the corner of Aleksoto and Muitinės Streets in Kaunas Old Town, Lithuania. It was a psychiatric hospital, but is now owned by the Kaunas Academy of Arts institute.

spots.name: Vytautas the Great Bridge
spots.summary: Vytautas the Great Bridge, also known as Aleksotas Bridge before 1930 and from 1940 until 23 February 2008, crosses the Nemunas River to connect Aleksotas and Old Town in Kaunas, Lithuania. Its length exceeds 256 meters, and its width is of 16 meters.

spots.name: Maironis Lithuanian Literature Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sun

spots.summary: The Maironis Lithuanian Literature Museum is located in the Siručiai Palace of Kaunas, Lithuania. It contains the former home of Lithuanian priest and poet Jonas Mačiulis-Maironis, who purchased the building in 1909. The museum opened in 1936.

spots.name: Kaunas Museum for the Blind

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Kaunas Museum for the Blind is an art and cultural museum in Kaunas, Lithuania that opened in 2005. It was the first museum for the blind in the Baltic States and one of the first in Eastern Europe.

spots.name: Kaunas State Musical Theatre
spots.summary: The Kaunas State Musical Theatre, formerly Kaunas City Theatre, is a theatre in Kaunas, Lithuania. It is home to a musical theatre company of the same name, established on 27 November 1940 in the former State Theatre hall on the Laisvės Alėja.

spots.name: Saint Nicholas Church
spots.summary: Church of Saint Nicholas (of Benedictine Sisters) (Lithuanian: Kauno Šv. Mikalojaus (Benediktinių) bažnyčia) is a Roman Catholic church in the Old Town of Kaunas, Lithuania.

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Former Communications History Museum was a museum supported by Teo LT AB, former AB Lietuvos Telekomas, in the Old Town of Kaunas, Lithuania. The building is an old merchant house, where were storages for grain to be exported.

spots.name: Kaunas Lutheran Holy Trinity Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Kaunas Lutheran Holy Trinity Church is a Lutheran church in the Old Town of Kaunas, Lithuania. It is one of the first Lutheran churches in Kaunas, built in 1683. The wooden main altar dates from 1692. The church was closed by the Soviet authorities, nowadays it used by the local university.

spots.name: Kaunas Picture Gallery
